We must create a project owner AI. The POAI (Project Owner AI) knows everything in detail about the project. POAI can answer any question almost immediately.
POAI assists users and other processes.

Carefully review the codx-junior api to see what already exists and define how to create the POAI module and how will work.

Optionally evaluate the possibility of small cpu llm models and finte tuning.

We expect:
 -  An AI that knows everything about the user project (so each project will have its own POAI)
 - Fast responses with support (wiki, text, image, mockups, slides, canva)
 - New profile POAI modulating llm nehavior that we can fine tune per project (if needed)
 - Optionally: New tools to help llm model to do its job.

I'll start by exploring the project structure to understand what already exists in the codx-api codebase.Let me read the most relevant files in detail to understand the existing architecture.Let me read the SmolAgent, knowledge training/loader, chat prompt builder, and tools to complete the picture.Let me examine the knowledge/Milvus layer, router discovery, and image engine to complete my understanding of extension points.Let me read the main chat engine and existing profile examples to finalize accurate extension points.I've completed a thorough review of the codebase. I now understand the existing architecture well enough to define the POAI module precisely. Below is my structured analysis, followed by the complete design document.

## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking

**Core Requirements**
- A per-project "Project Owner AI" (POAI) that knows everything about a specific user project.
- Fast responses with multiple output formats: wiki, text, image, mockups, slides, canva.
- A new `poai` profile that modulates LLM behavior and is fine-tunable per project.
- Optional new tools to help the LLM do its job.

**Strategic Approach**
Most of the required foundation **already exists** in codx-junior. POAI is essentially a *composition* of existing subsystems plus a thin orchestration layer:

| Requirement | Already exists | Gap to fill |
|---|---|---|
| Per-project knowledge | `Knowledge` (Milvus), `KnowledgeLoader`, `KnowledgeDB`, `project_summary.md`, wiki indexing | A dedicated "Project Owner context bundle" + fast retrieval path |
| Profiles that modulate behavior | `Profile` model, `ProfileManager`, linked profiles, per-project profile folders, `api_settings` | A new `poai.profile` (built-in + per-project override) |
| LLM behavior / per-project model | `Profile.llm_model`, `AIModel`, `get_model_settings` | A dedicated fast-path model (small/CPU) + fine-tune hooks |
| Tools | `TOOLS` registry (`project_search`, `project_read_file`, `generate_image`, `explain_image`, browser, etc.) | POAI-specific tools (mockups, slides, canva spec) |
| Output formats | `WikiManager` (wiki), `ImageEngine` (image), markdown chat (text) | Mockups/slides/canva renderers |
| API surface | `discover_routers()` auto-loads any `api/*.py` with a `router` | A new `api/poai.py` router |
| Fine-tuning | `KnowledgeTrainning` stub + `knowledge_generate_training_dataset` flag (already generates Q&A JSON) | Implement actual fine-tuning pipeline (LoRA/QLoRA or provider API) |
| Small CPU LLM | `ai/ollama.py` (llmfactory), `ai/vllm_cpu_ai.py` (deprecated), `SmolAgent` | Evaluate + wire a small model for the fast path |

**Dependencies & Risks**
- Small models have **weak tool-calling**. Mitigation: use small model only for read-only fast Q&A (no tools); keep the large model for agentic/code tasks.
- "Knows everything" is bounded by what's indexed. POAI must auto-bootstrap indexing from `project_summary.md`, `wiki_index.json`, dependency graph, and domain map.
- Fine-tuning cost/complexity is high relative to benefit when RAG + profile already works. Recommendation: ship RAG + profile first; fine-tuning is optional/offline.

**Target Files**
- Create: `codx/junior/poai/README.md` (this design document — the deliverable).

---

## 2. Minimum Changes Approach

This is a **design definition** task, not a code implementation. I will produce a single, self-contained design document that:
1. Maps the requirements to existing code.
2. Defines the new POAI module layout and behavior.
3. Evaluates small CPU LLMs and fine-tuning.

No existing files are modified.

---

"""
SmolAgent: a small, async-only OpenAI chat agent.

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to
      :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext`,
    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Vision API Support
Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged
VERBATIM: phase, model, provider, endpoint, whether an API key is configured,
message/tool counts, request/chat/run identifiers, HTTP status, provider
``code``/``param``/``request_id``, provider request-id header, response body
(truncated) and the chained root cause (``httpx.ConnectError``, DNS, TLS,
timeout, proxy, ...) — always followed by a full traceback. A short Markdown
notice with the same details is also streamed to the client, because previously
a failed connection surfaced as nothing more than the provider's generic
``"Connection error."`` string in both the logs and the chat.

"""
Tools module for codx-junior API.

This module aggregates all available tools for chat and project interactions.
Tools are organized as callable functions with associated metadata for
integration with language models and the API.

Tool Scope Levels:
    - "global": Tools always included in conversations (e.g., code_block_generator)
    - "chat": Tools available based on conversation context and selection

Tool Response Types:
    - str: Traditional single-string response (used for LLM context)
    - ToolResponse: Dual-return object for tools that need to produce both
                    user-facing content and LLM feedback

Glob Patterns:
    Glob patterns are only supported by search tools that return file paths
    (e.g. ``project_search``). Reading tools always use literal paths.
    Glob wildcards are:
        - ``*``   matches any characters within a single path segment
        - ``?``   matches a single character
        - ``[abc]`` matches one character from the set
        - ``**``  matches across multiple directories (recursive)
